subject: I-O status 24 (manner in which the boundaries of a file are defined)
notes: NOW (kb/Work PB3335, the whole-store model's remains deleted): both halves of the determination are the keyed store engine's (DESIGN-runtime-library 2.2.1.9). kb/Work PB1192 (w61d). A.1 item 107 required + documented; cite.py --check 9.1.13.5 'The implementor specifies the manner in which these boundaries are defined' -> OK 4). The section 7 determination: the boundary is the host file system's maximum file size, capped by the format at 2^32 pages of 4 096 bytes (PagedFile.FormatPages), met at the statement (PagedFile.Reserve, and a page write the host refuses to grow the file for (HandlePageMedium.Write asks HostFile.IsFileSizeLimit: ERROR_FILE_TOO_LARGE / EFBIG, raised as MediumSizeLimitException and answered by PagedFile.TryWrite)), and the relative key's own range is RelativeConnector.HighestRelativeRecordNumber; witnessed by the golden and the unit tests of FileBoundaryTests. KeyedConnector.RecordWriteFailed gives StoreStatus.Boundary '24' at a record WRITE or REWRITE alone, and KeyedConnector.Failed '30' at a DELETE, an OPEN or a CLOSE (section 9.1.13.6 item 1, no invalid key condition). retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/RecordFraming.cs#WriteStore (kb/Work PB2660 split the store write into ComposeStore (the framing) and KeyedConnector.Persist (the positional I/O);
